_about: The paper's bibliography. Cite with [@key] in paper/sections/*.html; build.py numbers the citations in order of first use, lists them, and writes paper/references.bib. 'role': used = CharForge runs it; compared = measured or weighed against ours; related = context. Every entry was checked against its source page on the date in 'checked'.

refs.title: Native and Compact Structured Latents for 3D Generation
refs.note: Published paper for the TRELLIS.2 model used in CharForge: 4B-parameter generation with O-Voxel latents; licensing for the actual model materials is separately recorded at trellis2license.

refs.title: TRELLIS.2 project materials and research-use notice
refs.note: The official page calls TRELLIS.2 a research project and says its page materials are solely for academic/research purposes and not intended for commercial exploitation. This is distinct from any code repository license; it does not alone resolve generated-output rights. Dynamic page checked 2026-09-26; footer copyright is not treated as a release year.

refs.title: Structured 3D Latents for Scalable and Versatile 3D Generation
refs.note: TRELLIS, the predecessor of TRELLIS.2.

refs.title: trellis2mlx: TRELLIS.2 on Apple Silicon (MLX)
refs.note: Upstream MLX port with CharForge's multi-view patch. On 2026-09-26 the local vendor checkout was at cddaf3cb8a9f28956114956ebe754d6661a3f695 with four modified tracked files and one untracked backup; this repository URL alone does not identify the local runtime source.

refs.title: Hunyuan3D 2.0: Scaling Diffusion Models for High Resolution Textured 3D Assets Generation
refs.note: An alternative image-to-3D generator (shape DiT + texture painter).

refs.title: Hunyuan3D 2.1: From Images to High-Fidelity 3D Assets with Production-Ready PBR Material
refs.note: Vendored in the repository for comparison. The paper does not establish that unnamed hosted products use this generator.

refs.title: CharacterGen: Efficient 3D Character Generation from Single Images with Multi-View Pose Canonicalization
refs.note: Four A-pose views from one image, a sparse-view reconstruction model, texture back-projection with depth test and Poisson blending; rigs with AccuRig. Anime3D dataset (13,746 VRoid models).

refs.title: Make-A-Character: High Quality Text-to-3D Character Generation within Minutes
refs.note: An LLM (Qwen-14B) parses the prompt into attributes; a portrait is generated and fitted onto MetaHuman topology with 431 dense landmarks; strand hair and library-matched garments; 52 blendshapes.

refs.title: Make-A-Character 2: Animatable 3D Character Generation From a Single Image
refs.note: Single portrait to animatable character in under 2 minutes: IC-Light relighting, colour correction, hierarchical face reconstruction, adaptive facial skeleton calibration.

refs.title: DrawingSpinUp: 3D Animation from Single Character Drawings
refs.note: Image-to-3D of a drawing, contour removal and restoration, skeleton-based thinning; rigs with Mixamo's auto-rigger (eight front-view keypoints) and nearest-bone weights, retargets with Rokoko. arXiv:2409.08615.

refs.title: Generation of 3D Human Models and Animations Using Simple Sketches
refs.note: A VAE from 2D stick figures to 3D point-cloud bodies, and animation by interpolating in its latent space.

refs.title: A Method for Animating Children's Drawings of the Human Figure
refs.note: 2D rigging of drawings; the baseline DrawingSpinUp compares against.

refs.title: Automatic Rigging and Animation of 3D Characters
refs.note: Embeds a template skeleton in a mesh and computes weights by heat diffusion.

refs.title: RigNet: Neural Rigging for Articulated Characters
refs.note: Learned joints, bone connectivity and skin weights.

refs.title: One Model to Rig Them All: Diverse Skeleton Rigging with UniRig
refs.note: Autoregressive skeleton prediction (skeleton tree tokenization) and skin weights; Rig-XL dataset of 14,000+ rigged models.

refs.title: AccuRIG: free automatic character rigging
refs.note: Official material supports marker-guided joint placement and configurable finger counts. CharacterGen reports using AccuRIG; the cited source does not substantiate a generic one-click skinning claim for every standalone workflow.

refs.title: PINOC AI auto-rigging
refs.note: The product guide describes guide markers and retargeting/mapping for compatible humanoid rigs; its finger controls concern mapping an existing rig, not a claim that PINOC generates finger bones on every output.

refs.title: Rig Lab: AI rigging
refs.note: Automatic humanoid joints and skinning from an A/T-pose GLB; hands are single joints (no fingers); four procedural clips. The checked page does not establish a release year.

refs.title: Mixamo FAQ
refs.note: Adobe's FAQ (updated 2021-09-14) says Mixamo characters/animations may be used royalty-free in personal, commercial and non-profit projects, including games. It does not identify CharForge's local mirror or by itself resolve redistribution of the mirror/raw clip files.

refs.title: Mixamo animation FBX mirror
refs.note: The dataset card identifies 2,453 animation FBXs downloaded from Mixamo. CharForge's cached snapshot at revision b1c7f4975ea3261d3d0aa2379f6e24754ccde9d8 independently contains 2,453 files in animation/; the mirror is not Adobe-authored and requires accepting conditions including sharing contact information. That count/access page does not establish redistribution permission.

refs.title: Turn Image to 3D Model Free - No Sign-Up Required
refs.note: The vendor page advertises free OBJ exports with selectable 5K-40K face-count choices; it does not substantiate rigging or animation. Free outputs are described as personal-use only, so check terms before project use or redistribution. Page checked 2026-09-26; that is not a release year.

refs.title: Cinevva 3D Model Generator
refs.note: The current workbench page advertises text or up to four views, rigging/animation and GLB export with 10K-1.5M triangles; it describes unnamed mesh engines and does not identify Hunyuan3D as its backend. Dynamic, undated vendor page; checked 2026-09-26.

refs.title: Best AI 3D Model Generators in 2026: Text-to-3D and Image-to-3D Compared
refs.note: Vendor editorial guide, published 2026-07-17 and updated 2026-09-14; its topology observations are not a controlled benchmark and it discloses the publisher sells a compared product.

refs.title: Qwen-Image Technical Report
refs.note: Technical report for the original Qwen-Image family, not documentation for the Qwen-Image 2.1 checkpoint used by CharForge.

refs.title: Qwen-Image-2.0 Technical Report
refs.note: Technical report for Qwen-Image 2.0 only; it does not document or license the separate 2.1 checkpoint.

refs.title: Qwen-Image-2.1
refs.note: Official repository documents the 7B visual-generation component, native RGBA transparency and ComfyUI support; released 2026-09-20. The exact license is cited separately.

refs.title: Qwen-Image-2.1 Qwen Research License Agreement
refs.note: The bundled license grants use, modification and distribution only for non-commercial research/evaluation; commercial use requires a separate license. Public source/weights should not be conflated with unrestricted commercial permission.

refs.title: Minimax-h3_Singularity Ref2VA fine-tune
refs.note: The model named by pipeline/motion_video.py: a community W4A8 Ref2VA fine-tune, converted/merged locally for inference. Its model card declares Apache-2.0 and identifies MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 as its base. The upstream MiniMax H3 agreement defines H3 Works to include model derivatives and its use policy covers outputs; compatibility/authorization is unresolved, not cleared by the card label.

refs.title: MiniMax H3 model card and Community License
refs.note: Official source links the Community License. The agreement defines H3 Works to include model derivatives; it excludes the US, EU, UK and Republic of Korea from the Applicable Territory, and its use policy restricts use/reproduction/distribution/display of Outputs outside that territory. It permits contacting MiniMax about separate authorization. The relationship to a fine-tune card declaring Apache-2.0 remains unresolved; this is not legal advice.

refs.title: MiniMax H3 Community License Agreement
refs.note: The primary license text, dated 2026-08-02, defines the Applicable Territory and H3 Works/Model Derivatives; section V and Exhibit A restrict use of Outputs outside the Applicable Territory. It says users in excluded territories may contact MiniMax regarding separate authorization. Read the full agreement; this citation is not legal advice.

refs.title: Comfy-Org MiniMax-H3 ComfyUI components
refs.note: CharForge's motion-video client loads the text encoder and VAEs from this packaging repository; it is not the W4A8 Ref2VA transformer checkpoint used for generation.

refs.title: ViTPose: Simple Vision Transformer Baselines for Human Pose Estimation
refs.note: 17-point body pose on video frames and on renders (checkpoint usyd-community/vitpose-base-simple).

refs.title: Effective Whole-body Pose Estimation with Two-stages Distillation
refs.note: 133 whole-body points; CharForge uses its 21-point hands.

refs.title: DINOv3
refs.note: TRELLIS.2's paper identifies DINOv3-L as its image-conditioning encoder; CharForge's local converter references a ViT-L/16 checkpoint, which should be separately pinned in run provenance.

refs.title: SegFormer: Simple and Efficient Design for Semantic Segmentation with Transformers
refs.note: SegFormer architecture paper; the actual FASHN-B4 human-parsing checkpoint and its NVIDIA Source Code License are documented separately at fashnparser.

refs.title: FASHN Human Parser
refs.note: Repository documents a SegFormer-B4 fine-tuned for 18-class human parsing and says the model inherits NVIDIA's Source Code License for SegFormer; review that license separately from the SegFormer paper citation.

refs.title: U²-Net: Going deeper with nested U-structure for salient object detection
refs.note: The U²-Net salient-object detector used through rembg for reference/video-frame cut-outs; this citation is not evidence of human-parser accuracy.

refs.title: Fast Optical Flow using Dense Inverse Search
refs.note: Aligns the reference to renders of the mesh during texture projection (OpenCV's DIS).

refs.title: Dynamic Programming Algorithm Optimization for Spoken Word Recognition
refs.venue: IEEE Transactions on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing 26(1)
refs.note: Dynamic time warping, for matching a video's pose sequence to library clips.

refs.title: Joint-Dependent Local Deformations for Hand Animation and Object Grasping
refs.note: Early joint-dependent local hand deformations for animation and grasping; this paper is not the source for the linear-blend skinning formula.

refs.title: Skinning with Dual Quaternions
refs.venue: ACM SIGGRAPH Symposium on Interactive 3D Graphics and Games (I3D)
refs.note: Dual-quaternion skinning reduces some volume-loss/collapse artifacts of linear blending; CharForge's E024 measurement still finds residual collapsed jacket faces.

refs.title: Contact-Aware Retargeting of Skinned Motion
refs.venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
refs.note: Retargets motion to a target character's skinned geometry while keeping self- and ground contacts and reducing interpenetration, with a learned geometry-conditioned network and encoder-space optimisation; CharForge's E128 addresses the same interpenetration with measured per-character joint limits instead of a learned model.

refs.title: Geodesic Voxel Binding for Production Character Meshes
refs.venue: ACM SIGGRAPH/Eurographics Symposium on Computer Animation (SCA)
refs.note: Skin weights from distances through the voxelised body, the idea CharForge's weights follow.

refs.title: SMPL: A Skinned Multi-Person Linear Model
refs.note: The parametric body most human-recovery methods fit; CharForge fits the character's own skeleton instead.

refs.title: Keep it SMPL: Automatic Estimation of 3D Human Pose and Shape from a Single Image
refs.note: Optimisation of a body model against 2D joints with priors - the analysis-by-synthesis idea the refine stage applies to the character's own mesh.

refs.title: End-to-end Recovery of Human Shape and Pose
refs.note: Regresses a 3D human body mesh with pose and shape from a single RGB image, not just a skeleton pose.

refs.title: Humans in 4D: Reconstructing and Tracking Humans with Transformers
refs.note: Video human mesh recovery and tracking - an alternative to our retrieval-and-fit.

refs.title: WHAM: Reconstructing World-grounded Humans with Accurate 3D Motion
refs.note: World-grounded 3D motion from video, with foot contact - a candidate replacement for depth borrowed from the library.

refs.title: Poisson Image Editing
refs.note: Gradient-domain blending, used at texture seams by CharacterGen and Make-A-Character.

refs.title: VDB: High-Resolution Sparse Volumes with Dynamic Topology
refs.note: General sparse VDB volume and level-set method. CharForge's use of level sets for solidification, arm cuts and hands is supported by project implementation, not presented as a result of this paper.

refs.title: Blender 5.2 command-line manual
refs.note: Version-pinned command-line/background-run documentation; the fact that CharForge scripts each listed stage is evidenced by repository implementation.

refs.title: ComfyUI
refs.note: Runs image and video workflows; this rolling repository citation is not an immutable revision for the specific CharForge environment.

refs.title: Ollama Gemma 4 E4B model tag
refs.note: CharForge's first-choice Ollama tag is gemma4:e4b; pipeline/describe.py permits environment/settings overrides and falls through to later models. The downloaded quantization/digest is not pinned here.

refs.title: glTF 2.0 Specification
refs.note: Defines the glTF package format and its weighted joint-transform linear-blend skinning path; it does not specify FBX behavior.

refs.title: three.js r160 (0.160.0)
refs.note: The playground's pinned WebGL renderer and animation mixer version (r160/0.160.0); the version-specific release is cited rather than the rolling homepage.

refs.title: TIFA: Accurate and Interpretable Text-to-Image Faithfulness Evaluation with Question Answering
refs.note: Fine-grained prompt-to-image attribute checks via generated questions and visual question answering; a candidate measurement pattern, not a validated scorer for stylized characters.

refs.title: GenEval: An Object-Focused Framework for Evaluating Text-to-Image Alignment
refs.note: Object-centric checks for co-occurrence, count, position, and color; useful for composing a character-specific prompt-fidelity test.

refs.title: Benchmarking and Learning Multi-Dimensional Quality Evaluator for Text-to-3D Generation
refs.note: MATE-3D: 1,280 textured meshes with human ratings separated into semantic alignment, geometry, texture, and overall quality; its evaluator should not be assumed to transfer to CharForge characters without calibration.

refs.title: THUman 2.0 Dataset
refs.venue: Project dataset and terms of use
refs.note: Pin the exact release: the current repository README also describes THUman2.1. The public release provides scan meshes/textures and rendering recipes, not a set of captured calibrated multi-view RGB views. Terms state non-commercial research use and restrict third-party sharing of scans or derived data without prior written permission; obtain permission or keep derived evaluation internal.

refs.title: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
refs.note: Unifies 15 marker-based mocap datasets as rigged SMPL sequences; broad exact-motion source for controlled renders, but it does not provide paired RGB video.

refs.title: Total Capture: 3D Human Pose Estimation Fusing Video and Inertial Sensors
refs.note: Synchronized calibrated video, IMU, and Vicon labels, including about 1.9 million frames; strong primary motion test but a small indoor participant/action cohort.

refs.title: Recovering Accurate 3D Human Pose in The Wild Using IMUs and a Moving Camera
refs.note: 3DPW supplies in-the-wild footage from a moving phone camera with IMU/video-derived pose labels; use it to test camera-motion generalization and document its annotation/alignment assumptions.

refs.title: AI Choreographer: Music Conditioned 3D Dance Generation with AIST++
refs.note: 1,408 dance sequences, ten genres, nine camera views; 3D motion is reconstructed from multi-view video, so use as an action-diversity stress set rather than Vicon-grade ground truth and exclude the dataset's ignore-list.

refs.title: Pose Space Deformation: A Unified Approach to Shape Interpolation and Skeleton-Driven Deformation
refs.note: Foundational pose-conditioned corrective deformation; supports E107's elbow/shoulder correctives, while the fitted examples and runtime constraints remain to be measured for CharForge.

refs.title: Expressive Body Capture: 3D Hands, Face, and Body From a Single Image
refs.note: SMPL-X jointly models hands, face, and body; the authors emphasize dense features and pose priors, useful context for E006/E109 but not a replacement template for arbitrary stylized meshes.

refs.title: Embodied Hands: Modeling and Capturing Hands and Bodies Together
refs.note: MANO learns pose-conditioned hand shape corrections from scans; models/data are research-access gated, so use as a methodological reference unless its terms fit.

refs.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Deep Features as a Perceptual Metric
refs.note: Introduces learned deep-feature perceptual comparison against human similarity judgments; use as a secondary held-out-view image metric, not a standalone geometry or animation score.

refs.title: glTF Validator
refs.note: Validates glTF 2.0 structure/resources and emits a JSON report; it does not prove Unity/Unreal/Godot-specific import or runtime behavior.

refs.title: Importing Model Files
refs.note: Documents Unity model, humanoid rig/clip, material, texture, and blend-shape importer behavior; pin the actual Unity version in the smoke fixture.

refs.title: FBX Skeletal Mesh Pipeline
refs.note: Documents FBX 2020.2, skeletal meshes, morph targets, LODs, and the single-animation-per-skeletal-mesh-file constraint relevant to package layout.

refs.title: Import Configuration
refs.note: Documents skin influence limits, material handling, animation sampling/grouping, and import-time options; pin the actual Godot release in the smoke fixture.

refs.title: Model Cards for Model Reporting
refs.note: Recommends documenting intended uses, evaluation procedures, performance characteristics, and limitations of released models; supports the dependency/provenance register, not a license interpretation.

refs.title: Datasheets for Datasets
refs.note: Proposes documenting dataset motivation, composition, collection, uses, and maintenance; a practical structure for CharForge's motion/scan evaluation provenance.

refs.title: DDH-QA: A Dynamic Digital Humans Quality Assessment Database
refs.venue: IEEE International Conference on Multimedia and Expo (ICME)
refs.note: Human study on 800 dynamic digital humans and ten motion types; explicitly includes binding error and motion unnaturalness, useful as an aberration taxonomy but not a trained scorer validated on stylized generated characters.

refs.title: DHQA-4D: A Large-Scale Dataset and LMM-Based Metric for Dynamic 4D Digital Human Quality Assessment
refs.note: 32 scanned dynamic humans, 11 distortion types, and human ratings including temporal discontinuity; a recent reference for E102's test taxonomy, not evidence that its evaluator transfers to CharForge.

refs.title: On Calibrating Semantic Segmentation Models: Analyses and an Algorithm
refs.note: Studies segmentation confidence calibration, including prediction correctness and domain shift; motivates retaining parser probabilities and calibrating abstention on CharForge-specific annotations rather than assuming softmax confidence is correctness.

refs.title: Metro: Measuring Error on Simplified Surfaces
refs.note: Surface-sampling method to compare a source surface with its simplified version; informs E118's area-sampled source-to-retopo distances, not a CharForge-specific acceptance threshold.

refs.title: ManifoldPlus: A Robust and Scalable Watertight Manifold Surface Generation Method for Triangle Soups
refs.note: Repairs triangle soups through voxel occupancy and projection while explicitly balancing watertight topology with resemblance to the input; motivates separate topology-success and shape-preservation measurements in E116.

refs.title: InterHand2.6M: A Dataset and Baseline for 3D Interacting Hand Pose Estimation from a Single RGB Image
refs.note: Real-captured single/interacting hand sequences with 3D pose labels; supports a subject-held-out check that separates image detector accuracy from retargeted hand articulation. Data terms/split must be pinned before use.

refs.title: UnderPressure: Deep Learning for Foot Contact Detection, Ground Reaction Force Estimation and Footskate Cleanup
refs.venue: Computer Graphics Forum 41(8), Symposium on Computer Animation
refs.note: Uses pressure-insole recordings as foot-contact evidence; supports a separately labeled contact benchmark, not a justification for deriving contact truth from CharForge's geometric floor threshold.

refs.title: A FACS Valid 3D Dynamic Action Unit Database with Applications to 3D Dynamic Morphable Facial Modeling
refs.note: Dynamic 3D facial action sequences with expert peak-frame FACS labels; useful for an expression challenge taxonomy, but human scans and AU labels do not directly validate stylized blendshape appearance.

refs.title: Instant Multi-View Head Capture Through Learnable Registration
refs.note: Introduces TEMPEH and FaMoS: the CVPR paper reports 93 subjects and 28 sequences. Data access requires agreement to its license; human face scans are references, not stylized target truth.

refs.title: Learning to Dress 3D People in Generative Clothing
refs.note: Learns pose- and garment-conditioned clothing geometry from scans; relevant to independent garment layers and pose variation, but not a runtime spring solver or stylized-character validation set.

refs.title: Learning Cloth Dynamics: 3D+Texture Garment Reconstruction Benchmark
refs.venue: NeurIPS Competition and Demonstration Track, PMLR 133
refs.note: CLOTH3D++ pairs animated dressed-human RGB sequences with dense 3D body/cloth and texture annotations; informs challenge design only and remains subject to dataset access terms.

refs.title: Texture Mapping Progressive Meshes
refs.note: Optimizes a shared parameterization across progressive meshes with attention to texture stretch; motivates measuring local UV distortion rather than island overlap/median density alone.

refs.title: Mipmaps
refs.note: Explains per-level texture downsampling and trilinear runtime sampling; motivates E120's distance/mip inspection rather than assuming a base-level gutter prevents runtime bleed.

refs.title: Ten Simple Rules for Reproducible Computational Research
refs.note: Practical guidance for archiving exact code/data and recording computational procedures; informs claim-to-artifact lineage in E121.

refs.title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
refs.note: Models provenance as entities, activities and agents with derivation relations; a conceptual structure for per-run lineage, not a compliance claim.

refs.title: Machine Learning Bill of Materials (ML-BOM)
refs.note: Defines structured inventory/provenance concepts for ML models and datasets; a candidate schema for dependency inventory, not a substitute for per-run artifacts or legal review.

refs.title: BVHTree Utilities
refs.note: Documents overlap as returning index pairs between trees and ray casts; a BVH overlap result alone is not a documented narrow-phase triangle-intersection verdict.

refs.title: Perceptual Evaluation of Footskate Cleanup
refs.venue: Eurographics/ACM SIGGRAPH Symposium on Computer Animation (SCA)
refs.note: Controlled perceptual study reports small footsliding detectable in most tested conditions; its mannequin, view and environment setup informs blind-rating stimuli, not a universal CharForge threshold.

refs.title: AU-Blendshape for Fine-grained Stylized 3D Facial Expression Manipulation
refs.note: Introduces AUBlendSet with 32 action units across 500 identities and stylized AU control; informs E124 challenge design, not a validated CharForge benchmark or unrestricted dataset/model license.

refs.title: Reliability in Semantic Segmentation: Are We on the Right Track?
refs.note: Evaluates segmentation robustness, calibration, misclassification detection and OOD detection; motivates confidence/abstention checks, but its natural-image datasets do not establish CharForge thresholds.
